fragments.quantifiers.formal: forall (s,delta) in D0: exists G_{s,delta} subset X^{s,delta}_vac(AF) with G_{s,delta} comeager: forall (Sigma,h,K) in G_{s,delta}, letting (M,g) be the maximal globally hyperbolic development: exists a conformal completion (Mtilde,gtilde,Omega) of (M,g) at I+ such that (i) I+ is null with I+ diffeomorphic to R x S^2, and (ii) every null geodesic generator of I+ is future-complete, and forall future-inextendible causal geodesics gamma of (M,g) with finite affine length: not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M.
fragments.quantifiers.domains.D5.definition: points q of I+ such that gamma([0,T)) is contained in the causal past J^-(q) intersected with M
fragments.visibility.definition: a future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma: [0,T) -> M with T < infinity in affine parameter is visible from I+ iff there exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M. Visibility is a property of the singular END of the geodesic, so the tail formulation is used; requiring the whole geodesic to lie in J^-(q) would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted]
fragments.visibility.negation_conclusion: there is NO visible_singularity_from_I_plus: for every future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma of finite affine length, for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail gamma([t0,T)) is NOT contained in J^-(q) intersect M - no single point of I+ causally precedes the singular end of gamma. This is NOT equivalent to 'gamma is contained in B = M minus J^-(I+)': B-containment is strictly stronger, and a geodesic may begin in J^-(I+) and end in the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted; the earlier 'i.e. inside B' equivalence was false]
